Nat.lt_succ.code: Nat.lt_succ {m n : ℕ} : m < n.succ ↔ m ≤ n
Nat.lt_succ.description: A natural number is less than the successor of another if and only if it is less than or equal to that number.

Nat.lt_succ_self.description: A natural number is always less than its successor.

Nat.lt.base.description: A natural number is always less than its successor.

Nat.lt_succ_iff.code: Nat.lt_succ_iff {m n : ℕ} : m < n.succ ↔ m ≤ n
Nat.lt_succ_iff.description: A natural number is less than the successor of another if and only if it is less than or equal to that number.

Nat.succ_le_of_lt.code: Nat.succ_le_of_lt {n m : ℕ} (h : n < m) : n.succ ≤ m
Nat.succ_le_of_lt.description: If a natural number is less than another, its successor is less than or equal to that other number.

Nat.succ_ne_zero.description: The successor of a natural number is never equal to zero.

Nat.succ_pred_eq_of_pos.description: If a natural number is positive, then the predecessor of that number, when increased by one, equals the original number.

Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add.code: Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add {n k m : ℕ} (H : n ≤ k) (h : k < n + m) : k - n < m
Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add.description: If a number is less than the sum of another number and a third number, then subtracting the first number from the second number will yield a result less than the third number, provided the first number is less than or equal to the second.

Nat.add_comm.code: Nat.add_comm (n m : ℕ) : n + m = m + n
Nat.add_comm.description: The addition of two natural numbers is commutative, meaning their order does not affect the sum.

Nat.sub_eq_iff_eq_add.code: Nat.sub_eq_iff_eq_add {b a c : ℕ} (h : b ≤ a) : a - b = c ↔ a = c + b
Nat.sub_eq_iff_eq_add.description: A natural number minus another is equal to a third number if and only if the first number is the sum of the second number and the third number.

Nat.add_assoc.code: Nat.add_assoc (n m k : ℕ) : n + m + k = n + (m + k)
Nat.add_assoc.description: The sum of three natural numbers is associative, meaning that the grouping of the numbers does not affect the result.

Nat.sub_add_cancel.code: Nat.sub_add_cancel {n m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : n - m + m = n
Nat.sub_add_cancel.description: Subtracting a natural number from another and then adding the subtracted number back results in the original number, provided that the first number is greater than or equal to the second.

Nat.succ_sub_succ_eq_sub.code: Nat.succ_sub_succ_eq_sub (n m : ℕ) : n.succ - m.succ = n - m
Nat.succ_sub_succ_eq_sub.description: The difference between the successors of two natural numbers equals the difference between the original numbers.

Nat.pos_of_ne_zero.description: A natural number is greater than zero if and only if it is not equal to zero.

Nat.add_one.description: Adding one to a natural number is equivalent to taking its successor.

Nat.add_succ.code: Nat.add_succ (n m : ℕ) : n + m.succ = (n + m).succ
Nat.add_succ.description: The sum of a natural number and the successor of another natural number is equal to the successor of their sum.

Nat.zero_add.description: Adding zero to a natural number does not change its value.

Nat.add_left_comm.code: Nat.add_left_comm (n m k : ℕ) : n + (m + k) = m + (n + k)
Nat.add_left_comm.description: The addition of three natural numbers is commutative with respect to the leftmost number, meaning that rearranging the first two numbers does not change the sum.

Nat.pred_succ.description: The predecessor of the successor of a natural number is equal to the original number.

Nat.lt_of_succ_lt_succ.code: Nat.lt_of_succ_lt_succ {n m : ℕ} : n.succ < m.succ → n < m
Nat.lt_of_succ_lt_succ.description: If the successor of one natural number is less than the successor of another, then the original first number is less than the original second number.

Nat.two_mul.description: Twice a natural number is equal to the sum of that number with itself.

Nat.mul_succ.code: Nat.mul_succ (n m : ℕ) : n * m.succ = n * m + n
Nat.mul_succ.description: Multiplying a natural number by the successor of another natural number is equal to adding the original multiplication of the first number with the second number to the first number itself.

Nat.lt_succ_of_le.code: Nat.lt_succ_of_le {n m : ℕ} : n ≤ m → n < m.succ
Nat.lt_succ_of_le.description: If a natural number is less than or equal to another, it is also less than the successor of that number.

Nat.zero_eq.description: Zero is equal to the natural number zero.

Nat.add_le_add_right.code: Nat.add_le_add_right {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) (k : ℕ) : n + k ≤ m + k
Nat.add_le_add_right.description: If one natural number is less than or equal to another, adding the same natural number to both will preserve that inequality.

Nat.le_add_left.code: Nat.le_add_left (n m : ℕ) : n ≤ m + n
Nat.le_add_left.description: A natural number is less than or equal to the sum of itself and another natural number.

Nat.add_right_comm.code: Nat.add_right_comm (n m k : ℕ) : n + m + k = n + k + m
Nat.add_right_comm.description: The sum of three natural numbers can be rearranged so that the first number remains at the front while the other two are swapped.

Nat.le_add_right.code: Nat.le_add_right (n k : ℕ) : n ≤ n + k
Nat.le_add_right.description: A natural number is always less than or equal to itself plus another natural number.

Nat.succ_eq_add_one.description: The successor of a natural number is equal to that number plus one.

Nat.mul_le_mul_right.code: Nat.mul_le_mul_right {n m : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m) : n * k ≤ m * k
Nat.mul_le_mul_right.description: Multiplying two natural numbers on the same side by a third natural number preserves the inequality between them.

Nat.le.intro.code: Nat.le.intro {n m k : ℕ} (h : n + k = m) : n ≤ m
Nat.le.intro.description: If the sum of two natural numbers equals a third natural number, then the first number is less than or equal to the third number.

Nat.sub_le.code: Nat.sub_le (n m : ℕ) : n - m ≤ n
Nat.sub_le.description: The difference between two natural numbers is less than or equal to the first number.

Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq.code: Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq {m n : ℕ} : m < n.succ ↔ m < n ∨ m = n
Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq.description: A natural number is less than the successor of another number if and only if it is either less than that number or equal to it.

Nat.pred_lt_pred.code: Nat.pred_lt_pred {n m : ℕ} : n ≠ 0 → n < m → n.pred < m.pred
Nat.pred_lt_pred.description: If a natural number is not zero and is less than another natural number, then its predecessor is also less than the predecessor of the second number.

Nat.pow_succ.code: Nat.pow_succ (n m : ℕ) : n ^ m.succ = n ^ m * n
Nat.pow_succ.description: Raising a natural number to the next power is equivalent to multiplying the number raised to the current power by the number itself.

Nat.le_zero.description: A natural number is less than or equal to zero if and only if it is equal to zero.

Nat.succ_le_succ_iff.code: Nat.succ_le_succ_iff {a b : ℕ} : a.succ ≤ b.succ ↔ a ≤ b
Nat.succ_le_succ_iff.description: A natural number is less than or equal to another if and only if its successor is less than or equal to the successor of that number.

Nat.zero_lt_of_ne_zero.description: A natural number is greater than zero if it is not equal to zero.

Nat.blt.fullDefinition: def blt (a b : Nat) : Bool :=   ble a.succ b
Nat.blt.description: The definition represents a Boolean value indicating whether one natural number is less than another.

Nat.sub_le_sub_right.code: Nat.sub_le_sub_right {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) (k : ℕ) : n - k ≤ m - k
Nat.sub_le_sub_right.description: If one natural number is less than or equal to another, then subtracting the same amount from both will maintain that inequality.

Nat.le_total.code: Nat.le_total (m n : ℕ) : m ≤ n ∨ n ≤ m
Nat.le_total.description: For any two natural numbers, one of them is less than or equal to the other.

Nat.pos_pow_of_pos.code: Nat.pos_pow_of_pos {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ) (h : 0 < n) : 0 < n ^ m
Nat.pos_pow_of_pos.description: If a natural number is positive, then any positive power of it is also positive.

Nat.le_of_add_le_add_right.code: Nat.le_of_add_le_add_right {a b c : ℕ} : a + b ≤ c + b → a ≤ c
Nat.le_of_add_le_add_right.description: If the sum of a natural number and another is less than or equal to the sum of the second and a different natural number, then the first natural number is less than or equal to the latter.

Nat.ne_of_gt.code: Nat.ne_of_gt {a b : ℕ} (h : b < a) : a ≠ b
Nat.ne_of_gt.description: If one natural number is greater than another, then the two numbers cannot be equal.

Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero.description: A natural number that is less than or equal to zero must be equal to zero.

Nat.add_sub_of_le.code: Nat.add_sub_of_le {a b : ℕ} (h : a ≤ b) : a + (b - a) = b
Nat.add_sub_of_le.description: The sum of a natural number and the difference between two natural numbers, where the first is less than or equal to the second, equals the larger number.

Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.description: A natural number is positive if and only if it is not equal to zero.

Nat.div_le_self.code: Nat.div_le_self (n k : ℕ) : n / k ≤ n
Nat.div_le_self.description: A natural number divided by another non-zero natural number is less than or equal to the original number.

Nat.div_lt_self.code: Nat.div_lt_self {n k : ℕ} (hLtN : 0 < n) (hLtK : 1 < k) : n / k < n
Nat.div_lt_self.description: A positive natural number divided by a natural number greater than one is strictly less than the original number.

Nat.div_zero.description: Dividing a natural number by zero results in zero.

Nat.mod_zero.description: The remainder of a natural number when divided by zero is the original number itself.

Nat.div_add_mod.code: Nat.div_add_mod (m n : ℕ) : n * (m / n) + m % n = m
Nat.div_add_mod.description: The sum of a natural number divided by another natural number multiplied by that divisor, plus the remainder of the division, equals the original number.

Nat.mod_lt.code: Nat.mod_lt (x : ℕ) {y : ℕ} : y > 0 → x % y < y
Nat.mod_lt.description: The remainder of a natural number when divided by a positive natural number is always less than the divisor.

Nat.div_one.description: Dividing a natural number by one yields the original number.

Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul.code: Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul (m n k : ℕ) : m / n / k = m / (n * k)
Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul.description: Dividing a natural number by two other natural numbers sequentially is equivalent to dividing it by the product of those two numbers.

Nat.mod_add_div.code: Nat.mod_add_div (m k : ℕ) : m % k + k * (m / k) = m
Nat.mod_add_div.description: The remainder of a natural number when divided by another, added to the product of that divisor and the quotient, equals the original number.

Nat.add_sub_cancel'.code: Nat.add_sub_cancel' {n m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : m + (n - m) = n
Nat.add_sub_cancel'.description: If a natural number is greater than or equal to another, the sum of that other number and the difference between the two equals the larger number.

Nat.sub_lt_self.code: Nat.sub_lt_self {a b : ℕ} (h₀ : 0 < a) (h₁ : a ≤ b) : b - a < b
Nat.sub_lt_self.description: If a natural number is positive and less than or equal to another, the difference between the second and the first is less than the second number.

Nat.sub_add_comm.code: Nat.sub_add_comm {n m k : ℕ} (h : k ≤ n) : n + m - k = n - k + m
Nat.sub_add_comm.description: The sum of a natural number and another number minus a third number is equal to the difference between the first and third numbers plus the second number, given that the third number is less than or equal to the first.

Nat.add_sub_cancel_right.code: Nat.add_sub_cancel_right (n m : ℕ) : n + m - m = n
Nat.add_sub_cancel_right.description: Subtracting a natural number from the sum of that number and another equals the original larger number.

Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le.code: Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : ∃ k, n = m + k
Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le.description: If one natural number is less than or equal to another, then there exists a natural number such that the larger number can be expressed as the sum of the smaller number and that natural number.

Nat.add_lt_add_of_lt_of_le.code: Nat.add_lt_add_of_lt_of_le {a b c d : ℕ} (hlt : a < b) (hle : c ≤ d) : a + c < b + d
Nat.add_lt_add_of_lt_of_le.description: If one natural number is less than another and a second is less than or equal to a third, then the sum of the first two numbers is less than the sum of the second two numbers.

Nat.lt_add_of_pos_left.code: Nat.lt_add_of_pos_left {k n : ℕ} : 0 < k → n < k + n
Nat.lt_add_of_pos_left.description: If a natural number is greater than zero, then adding it to another natural number results in a sum that is greater than the second number.

Nat.bitwise.code: Nat.bitwise (f : Bool → Bool → Bool) (n m : ℕ) : ℕ
Nat.bitwise.fullDefinition: def bitwise (f : Bool → Bool → Bool) (n m : Nat) : Nat :=   if n = 0 then     if f false true then m else 0   else if m = 0 then     if f true false then n else 0   else     let n' := n / 2     let m' := m / 2     let b₁ := n % 2 = 1     let b₂ := m % 2 = 1     let r  := bitwise f n' m'     if f b₁ b₂ then       r+r+1     else       r+r decreasing_by apply bitwise_rec_lemma; assumption
Nat.bitwise.description: The bitwise operation on two natural numbers is defined using a binary function that combines their corresponding bits based on boolean logic.

Nat.shiftRight.fullDefinition: def shiftRight : @& Nat → @& Nat → Nat   | n, 0 => n   | n, succ m => shiftRight n m / 2
Nat.shiftRight.description: The right bitwise shift operation on a natural number is defined, taking a number and a shift value to produce a new natural number.

Nat.testBit.comment: `testBit m n` returns whether the `(n+1)` least significant bit is `1` or `0`
Nat.testBit.fullDefinition: def testBit (m n : Nat) : Bool :=   -- `1 &&& n` is faster than `n &&& 1` for big `n`.   1 &&& (m >>> n) != 0
Nat.testBit.description: The operation checks if the specified bit in a natural number is set to one or zero, based on its position.

Nat.gcd.comment:
Computes the greatest common divisor of two natural numbers.

This reference implementation via the Euclidean algorithm
is overridden in both the kernel and the compiler to efficiently
evaluate using the "bignum" representation (see `Nat`).
The definition provided here is the logical model
(and it is soundness-critical that they coincide).

The GCD of two natural numbers is the largest natural number
that divides both arguments.
In particular, the GCD of a number and `0` is the number itself:
```
example : Nat.gcd 10 15 = 5 := rfl
example : Nat.gcd 0 5 = 5 := rfl
example : Nat.gcd 7 0 = 7 := rfl
```
Nat.gcd.fullDefinition: def gcd (m n : @& Nat) : Nat :=   if m = 0 then     n   else     gcd (n % m) m   termination_by m   decreasing_by simp_wf; apply mod_lt _ (zero_lt_of_ne_zero _); assumption
Nat.gcd.description: The greatest common divisor of two natural numbers is defined as the largest natural number that divides both of them.

Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero.code: Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero (m n : ℕ) : m ∣ n ↔ n % m = 0
Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero.description: A natural number divides another if and only if the remainder when the second number is divided by the first is zero.

Nat.mul_div_cancel'.code: Nat.mul_div_cancel' {n m : ℕ} (H : n ∣ m) : n * (m / n) = m
Nat.mul_div_cancel'.description: If a natural number divides another, then multiplying it by the quotient of the second number divided by the first equals the second number.

Nat.decidable_dvd.code: Nat.decidable_dvd : DecidableRel fun x x_1 => x ∣ x_1
Nat.decidable_dvd.description: The divisibility relation among natural numbers is decidable.

Nat.le_of_dvd.code: Nat.le_of_dvd {m n : ℕ} (h : 0 < n) : m ∣ n → m ≤ n
Nat.le_of_dvd.description: If a positive natural number divides another, then the divisor is less than or equal to the dividend.

Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero.code: Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero {m n : ℕ} (H : n % m = 0) : m ∣ n
Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero.description: If the remainder of a division of one natural number by another is zero, then the first number divides the second.

Nat.lcm.comment: The least common multiple of `m` and `n`, defined using `gcd`.
Nat.lcm.fullDefinition: def lcm (m n : Nat) : Nat := m * n / gcd m n
Nat.lcm.description: The least common multiple of two natural numbers is defined in terms of their greatest common divisor.

Nat.dvd_lcm_left.code: Nat.dvd_lcm_left (m n : ℕ) : m ∣ m.lcm n
Nat.dvd_lcm_left.description: A natural number divides the least common multiple of itself and another natural number.

Nat.dvd_lcm_right.code: Nat.dvd_lcm_right (m n : ℕ) : n ∣ m.lcm n
Nat.dvd_lcm_right.description: A natural number divides the least common multiple of itself and another natural number.

Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul.code: Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul {m n k : ℕ} (h : m < n * k) : m / n < k
Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul.description: If one natural number is less than the product of two others, then that number divided by the first is less than the second.

Int.sign.comment:
Returns the "sign" of the integer as another integer: `1` for positive numbers,
`-1` for negative numbers, and `0` for `0`.
Int.sign.fullDefinition: def sign : Int → Int   | Int.ofNat (succ _) => 1   | Int.ofNat 0 => 0   | -[_+1]      => -1
Int.sign.description: This describes a function that outputs `1` for positive integers, `-1` for negative integers, and `0` for zero.

Int.ofNat.comment: A natural number is an integer (`0` to `∞`).
Int.ofNat.description: This asserts that every natural number can be represented as an integer.

Int.negSucc.comment:
The negation of the successor of a natural number is an integer
(`-1` to `-∞`).
Int.negSucc.description: This states that the negation of the successor of any natural number is an integer that ranges from `-1` to negative infinity.

Int.toNat.comment:
Turns an integer into a natural number, negative numbers become
`0`.

```
#eval (7 : Int).toNat -- 7
#eval (0 : Int).toNat -- 0
#eval (-7 : Int).toNat -- 0
```
Int.toNat.fullDefinition: def toNat : Int → Nat   | ofNat n   => n   | negSucc _ => 0
Int.toNat.description: This defines a function that converts an integer to a natural number, treating negative integers as zero.

Int.cast.code: Int.cast.{u} {R : Type u} [IntCast R] : ℤ → R
Int.cast.comment:
Apply the canonical homomorphism from `Int` to a type `R` from an `IntCast R` instance.

In Mathlib there will be such a homomorphism whenever `R` is an additive group with a `1`.
Int.cast.fullDefinition: @[coe, reducible, match_pattern] protected def Int.cast {R : Type u} [IntCast R] : Int → R :=   IntCast.intCast
Int.cast.description: This defines a function that maps integers to another type, provided there exists a specific structure in that type allowing such a conversion.

Int.natAbs.comment:
Absolute value (`Nat`) of an integer.

```
#eval (7 : Int).natAbs -- 7
#eval (0 : Int).natAbs -- 0
#eval (-11 : Int).natAbs -- 11
```

Implemented by efficient native code.
Int.natAbs.fullDefinition: def natAbs (m : @& Int) : Nat :=   match m with   | ofNat m => m   | -[m +1] => m.succ
Int.natAbs.description: This defines a function that returns the absolute value of an integer as a natural number.

IntCast.mk.code: IntCast.mk.{u} {R : Type u} (intCast : ℤ → R) : IntCast R
IntCast.mk.description: This establishes a construction method for creating an instance of a specific type that defines a way to map integers to that type.

Int.ofNat_eq_coe.description: This theorem asserts that the conversion of a natural number to an integer is equivalent to its natural number representation as an integer.

Int.ofNat.inj.code: Int.ofNat.inj : ∀ {a a_1 : ℕ}, Int.ofNat a = Int.ofNat a_1 → a = a_1
Int.ofNat.inj.description: This establishes that if two natural numbers are converted to integers and yield the same integer, then the original natural numbers must also be equal.

Int.negOfNat.fullDefinition: def negOfNat : Nat → Int   | 0      => 0   | succ m => negSucc m
Int.negOfNat.description: This defines a function that takes a natural number and returns its negation as an integer.

Ne.eq_1.code: Ne.eq_1.{u} {α : Sort u} (a b : α) : (a ≠ b) = ¬a = b
Ne.eq_1.description: This theorem states that the inequality of two elements is equivalent to the negation of their equality.

Int.le_toNat.code: Int.le_toNat {n : ℕ} {z : ℤ} (h : 0 ≤ z) : n ≤ z.toNat ↔ ↑n ≤ z
Int.le_toNat.description: This theorem expresses that a non-negative integer is less than or equal to the natural representation of a non-negative integer if and only if the integer itself is greater than or equal to its natural representation.

Int.sign_zero.description: This theorem states that the sign of zero is equal to zero.

Int.toNat_of_nonneg.description: This theorem states that a non-negative integer is equal to its natural number representation.

Int.neg_nonneg_of_nonpos.description: This theorem states that if an integer is less than or equal to zero, then its negation is greater than or equal to zero.

Int.toNat_zero.description: This theorem states that the natural representation of zero as an integer is equal to zero.

Int.sign_neg.description: This theorem states that the sign of the negative of an integer is equal to the negative of the sign of that integer.

Int.mul_nonneg.code: Int.mul_nonneg {a b : ℤ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) : 0 ≤ a * b
Int.mul_nonneg.description: This theorem states that the product of two non-negative integers is also a non-negative integer.

Int.ofNat_zero_le.description: This theorem states that any natural number is greater than or equal to zero in its integer representation.

Int.natAbs_eq_zero.description: This theorem states that the absolute value of an integer is zero if and only if the integer itself is zero.

Int.natAbs_negSucc.description: This theorem states that the absolute value of the negative successor of a natural number is equal to the successor of that natural number.

Int.natAbs_of_nonneg.description: This theorem states that the absolute value of a non-negative integer is equal to the integer itself.

Int.ofNat_lt.description: This theorem states that the inequality between two natural numbers holds if and only if the corresponding integers obtained from those natural numbers are also in the same order.

Int.natAbs_ne_zero.description: This theorem states that the absolute value of an integer is non-zero if and only if the integer itself is non-zero.

Int.sub_le_self.code: Int.sub_le_self (a : ℤ) {b : ℤ} (h : 0 ≤ b) : a - b ≤ a

Int.ofNat_natAbs_of_nonpos.description: This theorem states that the absolute value of a non-positive integer is equal to the negation of that integer.

Int.gcd.comment: Computes the greatest common divisor of two integers, as a `Nat`.

Int.neg_neg.description: This theorem states that the negation of the negation of an integer is equal to the original integer.

Int.negSucc_coe.description: This theorem states that the negative successor of a natural number is equal to the negation of its successor when represented as an integer.

Int.sub_add_cancel.code: Int.sub_add_cancel (a b : ℤ) : a - b + b = a
Int.sub_add_cancel.description: This theorem states that subtracting an integer from another and then adding the subtracted integer back yields the original integer.

Int.add_left_neg.description: This theorem states that adding the negation of an integer to the integer itself results in zero.

Int.add_right_neg.description: This theorem states that adding an integer to its negation results in zero.

Int.zero_emod.description: This theorem asserts that the remainder of zero divided by any integer is zero.

Int.add_mul_emod_self.code: Int.add_mul_emod_self {a b c : ℤ} : (a + b * c) % c = a % c
Int.add_mul_emod_self.description: This theorem states that the remainder of the sum of an integer and the product of another integer with a third integer, when divided by the third integer, equals the remainder of the first integer when divided by the same third integer.

Int.zero_ediv.description: This theorem states that dividing zero by any integer results in zero.

Int.emod_nonneg.code: Int.emod_nonneg (a : ℤ) {b : ℤ} : b ≠ 0 → 0 ≤ a % b
