Array.map.code: Array.map.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (as : Array α) : Array β
Array.map.fullDefinition: def map {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (as : Array α) : Array β :=   Id.run <| as.mapM f
Array.map.description: This defines a function that applies a transformation to each element of an array, producing a new array of a potentially different type.

Array.foldlM.code:
Array.foldlM.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {m : Type v → Type w} [Monad m] (f : β → α → m β) (init : β)
  (as : Array α) (start : ℕ := 0) (stop : ℕ := as.size) : m β
Array.foldlM.fullDefinition: def foldlM {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {m : Type v → Type w} [Monad m] (f : β → α → m β) (init : β) (as : Array α) (start := 0) (stop := as.size) : m β :=   let fold (stop : Nat) (h : stop ≤ as.size) :=     let rec loop (i : Nat) (j : Nat) (b : β) : m β := do       if hlt : j < stop then         match i with         | 0    => pure b         | i'+1 =>           have : j < as.size := Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le hlt h           loop i' (j+1) (← f b as[j])       else         pure b     loop (stop - start) start init   if h : stop ≤ as.size then     fold stop h   else     fold as.size (Nat.le_refl _)
Array.foldlM.description: This defines a function that accumulates a value from an array using a monadic operation while iterating from a specified start to stop index.

Array.isEmpty.code: Array.isEmpty.{u} {α : Type u} (a : Array α) : Bool
Array.isEmpty.fullDefinition: @[simp] def isEmpty (a : Array α) : Bool :=   a.size = 0
Array.isEmpty.description: This defines a function that checks whether an array is empty.

Array.foldrM.code:
Array.foldrM.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {m : Type v → Type w} [Monad m] (f : α → β → m β) (init : β)
  (as : Array α) (start : ℕ := as.size) (stop : ℕ := 0) : m β
Array.foldrM.fullDefinition: def foldrM {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {m : Type v → Type w} [Monad m] (f : α → β → m β) (init : β) (as : Array α) (start := as.size) (stop := 0) : m β :=   let rec fold (i : Nat) (h : i ≤ as.size) (b : β) : m β := do     if i == stop then       pure b     else match i, h with       | 0, _   => pure b       | i+1, h =>         have : i < as.size := Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.lt_succ_self _) h         fold i (Nat.le_of_lt this) (← f as[i] b)   if h : start ≤ as.size then     if stop < start then       fold start h init     else       pure init   else if stop < as.size then     fold as.size (Nat.le_refl _) init   else     pure init
Array.foldrM.description: This defines a function that folds an array from the right using a given monadic operation, producing a final accumulated value within a monadic context.

List.drop.eq_1.code: List.drop.eq_1.{u} {α : Type u} : ∀ (x : List α), List.drop 0 x = x
List.drop.eq_1.description: This theorem asserts that dropping zero elements from a list results in the original list itself.

Array.toList.code: Array.toList.{u} {α : Type u} (as : Array α) : List α
Array.toList.comment: Convert a `Array α` into an `List α`. This is O(n) in the size of the array.
Array.toList.fullDefinition: def toList (as : Array α) : List α :=   as.foldr List.cons []
Array.toList.description: This defines a function that converts an array into a list.

Array.filter.code: Array.filter.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (p : α → Bool) (as : Array α) (start : ℕ := 0) (stop : ℕ := as.size) : Array α
Array.filter.fullDefinition: def filter (p : α → Bool) (as : Array α) (start := 0) (stop := as.size) : Array α :=   as.foldl (init := #[]) (start := start) (stop := stop) fun r a =>     if p a then r.push a else r
Array.filter.description: This defines a function that filters elements of an array based on a given predicate, returning a new array of elements that satisfy the condition.

Array.mapM.code:
Array.mapM.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {m : Type v → Type w} [Monad m] (f : α → m β) (as : Array α) :
  m (Array β)
Array.mapM.fullDefinition: def mapM {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {m : Type v → Type w} [Monad m] (f : α → m β) (as : Array α) : m (Array β) :=   -- Note: we cannot use `foldlM` here for the reference implementation because this calls   -- `bind` and `pure` too many times. (We are not assuming `m` is a `LawfulMonad`)   let rec map (i : Nat) (r : Array β) : m (Array β) := do     if hlt : i < as.size then       map (i+1) (r.push (← f as[i]))     else       pure r   termination_by as.size - i   decreasing_by simp_wf; decreasing_trivial_pre_omega   map 0 (mkEmpty as.size)
Array.mapM.description: This defines a function that applies a monadic transformation to each element of an array, producing a new array within a monadic context.

Array.erase.code: Array.erase.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [BEq α] (as : Array α) (a : α) : Array α
Array.erase.fullDefinition: def erase [BEq α] (as : Array α) (a : α) : Array α :=   match as.indexOf? a with   | none   => as   | some i => as.feraseIdx i
Array.erase.description: This defines a function that removes all occurrences of a specified element from an array.

Array.filterMapM.code:
Array.filterMapM.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1 → Type u_2} {α : Type u_3} {β : Type u_1} [Monad m]
  (f : α → m (Option β)) (as : Array α) (start : Nat := 0) (stop : Nat := as.size) : m (Array β)
Array.filterMapM.fullDefinition: def filterMapM [Monad m] (f : α → m (Option β)) (as : Array α) (start := 0) (stop := as.size) : m (Array β) :=   as.foldlM (init := #[]) (start := start) (stop := stop) fun bs a => do     match (← f a) with     | some b => pure (bs.push b)     | none   => pure bs
Array.filterMapM.description: This defines a function that filters and maps an array using a monadic operation to produce a new array of optional values.

Array.any.code: Array.any.{u} {α : Type u} (as : Array α) (p : α → Bool) (start : Nat := 0) (stop : Nat := as.size) : Bool
Array.any.fullDefinition: def any (as : Array α) (p : α → Bool) (start := 0) (stop := as.size) : Bool :=   Id.run <| as.anyM p start stop
Array.any.description: This defines a function that determines if any elements in an array satisfy a given predicate within a specified range.

Array.contains.code: Array.contains.{u} {α : Type u} [BEq α] (as : Array α) (a : α) : Bool
Array.contains.fullDefinition: def contains [BEq α] (as : Array α) (a : α) : Bool :=   as.any (· == a)
Array.contains.description: This defines a function that checks whether an array contains a specific element based on an equality condition.

Array.swapAt!.code: Array.swapAt!.{u} {α : Type u} (a : Array α) (i : Nat) (v : α) : α × Array α
Array.swapAt!.fullDefinition: def swapAt! (a : Array α) (i : Nat) (v : α) : α × Array α :=   if h : i < a.size then     swapAt a ⟨i, h⟩ v   else     have : Inhabited α := ⟨v⟩     panic! ("index " ++ toString i ++ " out of bounds")
Array.swapAt!.description: This defines a function that replaces an element at a specified index in an array with a new value and returns the updated array along with the original element that was replaced.

Array.qsort.code: Array.qsort.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (as : Array α) (lt : α → α → Bool) (low : ℕ := 0) (high : ℕ := as.size - 1) : Array α
Array.qsort.fullDefinition: @[inline] partial def qsort (as : Array α) (lt : α → α → Bool) (low := 0) (high := as.size - 1) : Array α :=   let rec @[specialize] sort (as : Array α) (low high : Nat) :=     if low < high then       let p := qpartition as lt low high;       -- TODO: fix `partial` support in the equation compiler, it breaks if we use `let (mid, as) := partition as lt low high`       let mid := p.1       let as  := p.2       if mid >= high then as       else         let as := sort as low mid         sort as (mid+1) high     else as   sort as low high
Array.qsort.description: This defines a function that sorts an array using the quicksort algorithm, based on a provided comparison function.

BitVec.mul.code: BitVec.mul {n : ℕ} (x y : BitVec n) : BitVec n

Multiplication for bit vectors. This can be interpreted as either signed or unsigned negation
modulo `2^n`.

SMT-Lib name: `bvmul`.
BitVec.mul.fullDefinition: protected def mul (x y : BitVec n) : BitVec n := BitVec.ofNat n (x.toNat * y.toNat) instance : Mul (BitVec n) := ⟨.mul⟩

Std.Format.join.description: This definition specifies a way to concatenate a list of formatted elements into a single formatted result.

Std.Format.paren.comment: Creates the format `"(" ++ f ++ ")"` with a flattening group.
Std.Format.paren.fullDefinition: @[inline] def paren (f : Format) : Format :=   bracket "(" f ")"
Std.Format.paren.description: This definition creates a formatted expression that surrounds a given formatted element with parentheses.

Std.Format.fill.comment: Alias for a group with `FlattenBehavior` set to `fill`.
Std.Format.fill.fullDefinition: def fill (f : Format) : Format :=   group f (behavior := FlattenBehavior.fill)
Std.Format.fill.description: This definition provides an alias for creating a formatted group with a specific behavior that fills its content.

Std.Format.joinSep.code: Std.Format.joinSep.{u} {α : Type u} [Lean.ToFormat α] : List α → Lean.Format → Lean.Format
Std.Format.joinSep.comment: Intersperse the given list (each item printed with `format`) with the given `sep` format.
Std.Format.joinSep.fullDefinition: def Format.joinSep {α : Type u} [ToFormat α] : List α → Format → Format   | [],    _   => nil   | [a],   _   => format a   | a::as, sep => as.foldl (· ++ sep ++ format ·) (format a)
Std.Format.joinSep.description: This definition describes a method for combining a list of elements into a formatted output, inserting a specified separator format between each element.

Std.Format.line.comment:
A position where a newline may be inserted
if the current group does not fit within the allotted column width.
Std.Format.line.description: This theorem identifies a formatting position where a newline can be added if the current content exceeds the available column width.

Std.Format.bracket.comment:
Create a format `l ++ f ++ r` with a flatten group.
FlattenBehaviour is `allOrNone`; for `fill` use `bracketFill`.
Std.Format.bracket.fullDefinition: @[inline] def bracket (l : String) (f : Format) (r : String) : Format :=   group (nest l.length $ l ++ f ++ r)
Std.Format.bracket.description: This definition creates a formatted expression that surrounds a given formatted element with specified left and right strings while using a flattening group behavior.

Std.Format.text.comment: A node containing a plain string.
Std.Format.text.description: This theorem defines a format node that represents a plain text string.

Std.Format.align.comment:
`align` tells the formatter to pad with spaces to the current indent,
or else add a newline if we are already at or past the indent. For example:
```
nest 2 <| "." ++ align ++ "a" ++ line ++ "b"
```
results in:
```
. a
  b
```
If `force` is true, then it will pad to the indent even if it is in a flattened group.
Std.Format.align.description: This theorem defines a formatting function that aligns content by either adding spaces or new lines based on the current indentation, with an option to force alignment within flattened groups.

Std.Format.group.code: Std.Format.group : Format → optParam Std.Format.FlattenBehavior Std.Format.FlattenBehavior.allOrNone → Format
Std.Format.group.comment: Creates a new flattening group for the given inner format.
Std.Format.group.description: This theorem introduces a method for creating a flattening group around a specified format, allowing for control over the behavior of the formatting process.

Std.Format.tag.comment: Used for associating auxiliary information (e.g. `Expr`s) with `Format` objects.
Std.Format.tag.description: This theorem defines a format that allows the association of auxiliary information with formatted objects using a natural number identifier.

Std.Format.append.description: This theorem describes the operation of concatenating two formatted objects to create a single formatted output.

Std.Format.nest.comment:
`nest n f` tells the formatter that `f` is nested inside something with length `n`
so that it is pretty-printed with the correct indentation on a line break.
For example, we can define a formatter for list `l : List Format` as:

```
let f := join <| l.intersperse <| ", " ++ Format.line
group (nest 1 <| "[" ++ f ++ "]")
```

This will be written all on one line, but if the text is too large,
the formatter will put in linebreaks after the commas and indent later lines by 1.
Std.Format.nest.description: This theorem defines a formatting function that specifies the indentation level for nested content, ensuring proper alignment when the content is displayed across multiple lines.

Std.Format.nil.description: This theorem defines an empty formatting structure.
